newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Daredevil bikers lose their wheels in Saigon.
newsitem.headline: Daredevil bikers lose their wheels in Saigon.

text.p: Police in Ho Chi Minh City said on Monday that 119 motorbikes were impounded at the weekend after hundreds of youths staged a wild night-time race through the streets of the city.
They declined to give details of arrests.
High-speed racing has become a common expression of rebelliousness among the communist country's increasingly affluent urban youth.

Suggested solutions to the problems have included fining offenders, impounding their bikes for lengthy periods, expelling them from schools and colleges and setting up a legal race track on the outskirts of the city, formerly known as Saigon.

The prime minister is reported to have suggested tougher restrictions on the import of fast motorbikes. There are now some two million motorbikes in Vietnam -- a country of 75 million people -- about half of which are in Ho Chi Minh City.
